_comment: A foot block's combat re-face against cavalry inside its ranks keeps the men in their places. A 60-man Infantry block (10 files by 6 ranks) stands on Hold facing north, and a brittle 14-horse Cavalry troop (morale 3) charges it from the north-east. The riders push into the block, so the bearing from the block's anchor to their centre is taken from inside its own footprint and names no front. On main 799b0bca each tick's small re-face (under the 75-degree snap threshold) turned the whole slot grid about the anchor with the heading: the men chasing their slots dragged the anchor, the bearing moved on, and the facing wound round from -90 to -152.7 degrees by tick 520 and -165.5 by tick 600. At ticks 520 and 580 six and three men had their slots across the block's centreline from them, and at tick 440 the anchor stood at 893.8, 842.5. Now, with the riders' centre inside its footprint in contact, the infantry holds its facing (-90 degrees throughout) and its grid stays where the men stand, as a block already does for a router streaming through it: no slot crosses the centreline at those ticks, and the anchor has not been dragged off its ground at tick 440 (900.2, 839.8). The riders' own re-faces are unchanged: a troop of horse keeps its front to follow. Static camera. Deterministic (scenario + seed + scripted input). Measured with full state dumps every 10 ticks on main 799b0bca and on this branch (Windows).
